newsitem.title: UK: UK's Tomkins plans share buyback.
newsitem.headline: UK's Tomkins plans share buyback.

text.p: British diversified group Tomkins Plc said on Monday it planned to return excess cash to shareholders "periodically" and planned an initial share buy back of up to 100 million pounds ($169.1 million) within three months.

The company, which said it was on course for further earnings and dividend growth, said it would ask shareholders at the next general meeting in September to renew its authority to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares.

Tomkins, an international group whose baking and specialised engineering activities include the British "Hovis" bread brand and Smith & Wesson handguns, said it was sitting on a cash pile of 617 million pounds ($1 billion).
It said it was aiming to improve the return on investment for shareholders and continue to deliver strong net cash flow.

Tomkins, announcing a 33.7 percent rise in annual pretax profit to 431.8 million pounds and a 15 percent dividend increase, said the current trading year had got off to a good start, backed by "sound" orderbooks.
The British group said it expected to derive increasing benefit from newly-acquired U.S. automotive and industrial products firm Gates Corp. Tomkins bought Gates last year for one billion dollars.
